summary.text: Dan Cox, a Republican Frederick County attorney and former member of the Maryland House of Delegates, lost the November 3, 2026 election for governor of Maryland to Wes Moore.
He was also the Republican nominee for governor in 2022, when he lost to Moore.

paragraphs.text: Cox was born in Washington, D.C., and raised in Frederick County.
He earned a bachelor's degree from University of Maryland Global Campus in 2002 and a J.D. from Regent University School of Law in 2006.
He has worked as an attorney with The Cox Law Center and as a high school teacher at Walkersville Christian Family Schools.
Cox represented District 4 in the Maryland House of Delegates from January 2019 to January 2023 and served on the Judiciary Committee.
He won the 2022 Republican nomination for governor and lost the general election to Wes Moore.
In 2026 he was again the Republican nominee, on a joint ticket with Rob Krop.
During the campaign, he emphasized tax and fee reductions, housing affordability and energy costs.
He received 31.9% of the vote to Wes Moore's 64.1%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
